label: Custom and other frameworks
summary: The fallback for custom, uploaded and unknown frameworks (the library's GCRF is the only one listed). With no catalog of its own, the practical start is the one management-system standards use: say why the framework is taken on, write the scope down, name an owner and a sponsor, and decide who assesses first and when.

requires_org.reason: The scope names the legal entities it covers, picked from the profile.
Sites inside the scope are picked from the profile.
Systems inside the scope are picked from the key systems list.
Every framework needs an executive who backs the work and approves the scope.

source.ref: ISO management-system practice, clauses 4.1 and 4.2 (issues and interested parties with their requirements), used here as the general pattern for why a framework is taken on

fields.label: Driver
fields.note: Why the organisation takes this framework on. A regulator or customer brings a deadline and often a named assessor; an internal or voluntary decision does not.

fields.label: Required by
fields.note: The regulator or customer that requires it, with the contract or clause reference. Auditors and the other party ask for it.

fields.label: Deadline
fields.note: Date set by the regulator or customer for compliance or attestation.

fields.label: Version used
fields.note: Edition or version of the framework being followed, so the scope and the assessment refer to the same text.

source.ref: ISO management-system scoping practice, clause 4.3 (boundaries, activities, locations, interfaces; documented; exclusions justified)

fields.label: Scope statement
fields.note: One written statement of what is covered, where and for whom, as clause 4.3 asks of a management system. Auditors and customers read it first.

fields.label: Entities
fields.note: Legal entities inside the scope, picked from the organisation profile.

fields.label: Sites
fields.note: Sites inside the scope. An assessor plans visits and sampling from this list.

fields.label: Systems
fields.note: Systems and services inside the boundary. Include the interfaces to systems outside it.

fields.label: Exclusions
fields.note: Anything inside the organisation left out, each with the reason. An unjustified exclusion draws a finding. Leave empty if nothing is excluded.

source.ref: ISO management-system practice, clause 5.3 (top management assigns and communicates roles) and clause 5 (leadership)

fields.label: Framework owner
fields.note: The person accountable for compliance with this framework day to day. Auditors and customers ask who it is.

fields.label: Sponsor
fields.note: The executive who backs the work and approves scope and risk acceptance. Top-management ownership is what auditors look for.

source.ref: Certification-body practice: an independent assessment is planned before the audit and repeats on a cycle (Stage 1 and Stage 2, annual surveillance)

fields.label: Assessed by
fields.note: Who judges compliance: the team itself, an internal function independent of the team such as internal audit, or an outside body. Customers and regulators usually expect more independence for higher stakes.

fields.label: Third-party assessor
fields.note: Name of the outside assessor or certification body. Name it early; it sets the scope data it will ask for.

fields.label: Internal reviewer
fields.note: The person or function that reviews. They should not review what they run.

fields.label: First assessment
fields.note: Planned date of the first assessment. It sets the pace of the work.

fields.label: Repeat cycle
fields.note: How often the assessment repeats. Certificates and attestations expire, and internal programmes drift without a cycle.

gate.label: A scope statement is written
gate.hint: Say what is covered, where and for whom.

gate.label: The scope names a site, system or unit
gate.hint: Pick at least one site, system or unit from the organisation profile.

gate.label: An owner is named
gate.hint: Name the person accountable day to day.

gate.label: A sponsor is named
gate.hint: Name the executive who backs the work.

gate.label: Owner and sponsor are different people
gate.hint: The sponsor backs; the owner runs.

gate.label: The first assessment falls before the deadline
gate.hint: Leave time to fix findings before the date set by the regulator or customer.
